hero.title: Civil Engineering (PG) in Mauritius
hero.subtitle: A Master’s in Civil Engineering is a postgraduate qualification for students interested in structural design, construction, geotechnical engineering, transportation systems, water resources and infrastructure development. It helps graduates deepen their technical knowledge and prepare for specialised engineering, project management and research roles. For Indian students exploring a **Master’s in Civil Engineering in Mauritius for Indian Students**, this programme offers a dedicated postgraduate option to consider.

overview: Good news for prospective students: Unlike some other engineering specialisations, Mauritius has a verified dedicated programme: the Master in Civil Engineering with specialisation in Structures and Public Works at the Université des Mascareignes. It is available to local and international students on a part-time basis.

faq.question: Is a Master’s in Civil Engineering available in Mauritius?
faq.answer: Yes. The Université des Mascareignes offers a Master in Civil Engineering with specialisation in Structures and Public Works. It is available part-time to local and international students.

faq.question: How long does the Master in Civil Engineering take?
faq.answer: UdM lists a three-year route for eligible BAC+3 Civil Engineering graduates and a 1.5-year route for eligible BAC+4 graduates entering at Semester 3\. The university must confirm your individual eligibility.

faq.question: What is the tuition fee for Civil Engineering in Mauritius?
faq.answer: UdM currently lists its tuition and registration fees for this programme as to be finalised. The one-off application fee is listed as MUR 700 or US\$25. Contact the university for the current tuition schedule and details about Civil Engineering Fees in Mauritius.

faq.question: Are English and French required for admission?
faq.answer: The published course information states that some modules are taught in English and others in French. Applicants must have passed both languages at high-school or university level, or hold an acceptable language-proficiency certificate. Confirm the documents accepted by UdM before applying.

faq.question: What careers can I pursue after a Master’s in Civil Engineering?
faq.answer: Depending on your specialisation and experience, potential roles include structural engineer, civil project engineer, construction engineer, geotechnical engineer, infrastructure consultant and construction project manager. Professional registration may be necessary for certain positions.
